subject: Forensic snapshot scaling, temporal slicing & on-demand export commitments
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@sentinelbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: audit@sentinelbank.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Forensic snapshot harvest & on-demand export capabilities

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our RFP we need a clear, scorable description of your ability to provide:

- On-demand forensic snapshots (point-in-time) for audit windows up to 7 years.
- Temporal slicing (e.g., extract tokens/events for arbitrary UTC ranges with millisecond granularity).
- Bulk export SLA: max time-to-delivery for 100 GB / 1 TB / 5 TB of audit data.
- Chain-of-custody / tamper-evidence guarantees and evidence formats.
- Delivery options (S3 presigned upload, Azure Blob, physical delivery).
- Any per-export throughput limits, throttling or cost contingencies.

Can you provide a short commitment and a sample timeline for a 1 TB export that must be delivered to our S3 bucket (us-west-2) with checksum/tamper evidence? If you have standard pricing or a ballpark, include that too.

Appreciate a response by EOD PT tomorrow (Thu).

Carlos
Head of Audit, Sentinel Bank

---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@sentinelbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forensic snapshot harvest & on-demand export capabilities

Carlos —

Thanks for the clear scope. Below is a concise, scorable response you can slot into the RFP. I added our operational caveats and a sample timeline for a 1 TB export to S3 (us-west-2).

Commitment summary (scorable bullets):
- On-demand point-in-time snapshots: supported for all tenant data and metadata. Snapshots preserve KV cache state and associated request/response audit lines. Retention: configurable up to 7 years (default 13 months).
- Temporal slicing: Supported. We can extract records by UTC time range with millisecond granularity. Export includes event-level timestamps and request identifiers.
- Bulk export SLA (time-to-delivery):
  - 100 GB: target 4–8 hours (typical 3–6 hours)
  - 1 TB: target 12–24 hours (typical 10–18 hours)
  - 5 TB: target 48–96 hours (typical 36–72 hours)
  - SLA window applies to exports initiated during business hours; off-hours queues are supported but may add latency.
- Chain-of-custody & tamper evidence: Exports include SHA256 checksums for individual objects, a signed export manifest (PKCS7) and an audit trail describing the export operator, request id, and job timeline. We can optionally provide an HSM-signed attestation for enterprise plans.
- Delivery options: S3 (presigned PUT or server-side push to customer bucket), Azure Blob, GCS, or encrypted rsync over VPN. For very large datasets we support multipart uploads and cross-region transfer with customer-provided egress endpoints.
- Throughput & throttling: Network egress limited by the customer's reserved bandwidth plan on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted tenants we provide a default egress cap (configurable in Dedicated). Large exports may be rate-limited to preserve production SLAs; expected throughput for a single export job is up to 300 MB/s aggregated under Dedicated.
- Cost notes: Exports are charged as a one-time export job fee + per-GB egress. Ballpark for a 1 TB export: job fee $2,500 + egress $0.09/GB (subject to region). Exact pricing will be quoted in the SOW.

Sample timeline for 1 TB export (target delivery to us-west-2 S3 via presigned PUT):
- T0 (export request received & validated): 0–30 min (includes RPO verification and policy checks).
- T1 (export job queued & resources provisioned): 30–120 min.
- T2 (data extraction & packaging): 4–12 hours (parallel workers, temporal slicing applied).
- T3 (upload & checksum verification): 2–6 hours (depends on egress bandwidth).
- T4 (attestation & manifest signing): 15–45 min.
- Total expected: 10–20 hours (target SLA 12–24 hours).

Attachments: forensic_export_spec_v1.pdf (format/manifest schema), retention_matrix_20260729.xlsx (retention tiers & default windows).

Operational caveats / risks:
- Exports that require additional transformations (PII redaction, advanced reformatting) will increase T2 by the transform time and may be queued.
- Legal holds or ongoing litigation can add coordination time for chain-of-custody verification with the customer legal team.
- Very large concurrent exports (multiple TBs across many jobs) may be scheduled to prevent interference with live serving; in those cases we commit to a prioritized queue and a named escalation contact.

If that looks good I can convert this into an RFP-ready paragraph and include the signed attestation options. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk the timeline.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@sentinelbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forensic snapshot scaling, temporal slicing & on-demand export commitments

Carlos / Jordan —

Adding a few operational clarifications that buyers frequently ask for, and a proposed escalation path in case an export encounters issues:

Operational clarifications:
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with one event per line plus accompanying manifest. We can also deliver Parquet on request (adds transform time).
- Retention windows are per-tenant; we support automatic expiration policies and legal-hold flags to suspend deletion. Restores from legal hold will incur standard restore fees.
- For customers on Redwood Dedicated or Private: we can ship an appliance-based snapshot (encrypted disk image) as an alternative for extremely large historic archives.

Escalation path (for inclusion in RFP):
1) Initial support triage (support ticket) — 4-hour response SLA for enterprise plan.
2) Named Technical Account Manager (TAM) escalation — 2-hour response.
3) On-call engineering engagement + export acceleration plan — 1-hour response for Critical P1.

If you want, Ben can include a sample export manifest (we already attached sample_s3_manifest.json) and a short checklist for pre-approved S3 principals to speed presigned flows.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference

---
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@sentinelbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: audit@sentinelbank.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 19:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forensic snapshot scaling, temporal slicing & on-demand export commitments

Jordan / Kimberly —

This is exactly what we needed. A few follow-ups before we finalize scoring:

1) Can you confirm the HSM-signed attestation workflow and whether you have a sample attestation artifact we can review?
2) For the 1 TB timeline you provided — is the typical case (10–18 hours) measured on Dedicated customers? We are interested in worst-case (hosted) and Dedicated numbers separately.
3) Please include a short clause we can paste into the SOW that guarantees delivery within 36 hours for 1 TB exports for Dedicated plans, with a credit schedule if missed.

If you can drop the attestation sample and the SOW clause by EOD PT tomorrow we can incorporate this into the RFP scoring matrix.

Carlos
